stories.headline: SK Hyper eyes $350B for massive South Korean data centre buildout
stories.confirmed_fact: SK Telecom subsidiary SK Hyper is in early-stage talks to fund a 15GW data centre expansion in South Korea by 2035, with the first 5GW phase estimated to cost $350 billion.
stories.why_it_matters: The scale of this investment highlights the immense capital requirements for AI infrastructure, though the company plans to pace spending based on actual tenant demand rather than committing the full amount upfront.
stories.interpretation: This suggests a cautious approach to the 'build it and they will come' model of AI infrastructure, prioritising iterative growth over speculative over-capacity in a market currently wary of AI returns.
stories.source_title: SK Telecom unit SK Hyper is in talks with tech firms and investors to finance 15GW of data center capacity in South Korea by 2035; the first 5GW will cost $350B (Bloomberg)

stories.headline: OpenAI dismissals linked to alleged internal leaks
stories.confirmed_fact: OpenAI fired three safety researchers on October 1, reportedly suspecting them of sharing internal model design details with external researcher Ryan Greenblatt via disappearing Signal messages.
stories.why_it_matters: The incident highlights ongoing internal friction regarding information security and transparency at a leading AI developer, though the dismissed researchers dispute the allegations, characterising their communications as legitimate professional collaboration.
stories.interpretation: The use of disappearing messages in a high-stakes corporate environment creates a classic 'he-said, she-said' scenario that complicates the narrative of internal safety culture versus intellectual property protection.
stories.source_title: OpenAI suspected the three fired researchers of leaking internal model designs to AI safety researcher Ryan Greenblatt, including via disappearing Signal chats (Wall Street Journal)

stories.headline: Anthropic uses Claude to find bugs in open-source code
stories.confirmed_fact: Anthropic and formal-methods firm Theorem used Claude to produce machine-checked proofs for 123 open-source software libraries, identifying hundreds of previously undetected bugs in RISC-V assembly code.
stories.why_it_matters: While the results demonstrate the potential for AI to assist in formal verification, the findings are limited to specific single-threaded static binaries and do not could support bug-freedom across broader software environments.
stories.interpretation: It is a clever use of LLMs to automate the tedious work of formal verification, but it is worth remembering that 'crash-freedom' in a lab setting is a long way from total system security.
stories.source_title: Anthropic says it partnered with Theorem to use Claude to formally prove security properties at the assembly level across 100+ real-world open-source libraries (Anthropic)

stories.headline: Greece to implement social media ban for under-15s
stories.confirmed_fact: The Greek parliament has passed legislation banning social media access for children under 15, effective January 1, 2027, with a two-month window for platforms to implement age-verification.
stories.why_it_matters: The law places the burden of enforcement on platforms, though its practical success will depend on the effectiveness of broader EU-wide age-verification frameworks.
stories.interpretation: Legislating age limits is straightforward on paper; building a reliable, privacy-preserving verification system that actually stops a determined teenager is a significantly more difficult technical and social challenge.
stories.source_title: Greece's parliament passes a bill to ban social media platforms for children under 15 from 2027 and gives companies two months to verify users' ages (Angeliki Koutantou/Reuters)

stories.headline: NVIDIA releases OpenShell for AI agent security
stories.confirmed_fact: NVIDIA has open-sourced OpenShell, a runtime designed to isolate AI agents using kernel-level controls and credential gateway routing to prevent agents from accessing raw API keys.
stories.why_it_matters: As autonomous agents become more common, managing their access to sensitive systems is a critical security gap, though this project is in early 0.1.x development and has not yet undergone independent verification.
stories.interpretation: It is a sensible step toward 'least privilege' for AI, but developers should treat this as a starting point for testing rather than a plug-and-play solution for agent safety.
stories.source_title: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents

practical_takeaway: When evaluating AI infrastructure or security tools, focus on the specific constraints of the deployment. Whether it is the iterative funding model of SK Hyper or the limited scope of formal verification in Anthropic's research, the most reliable results come from understanding exactly where the technology stops working.
watch_next: Keep an eye on how the EU-wide age-verification frameworks evolve in response to Greece's new law, as this will likely set the precedent for how platforms handle similar mandates across other member states.
